findings.source: PythLazer.sol: TrustedSignerInfo[100] public trustedSigners; (slot 0, struct {address pubkey; uint256 expiresAt}); trustedSigners[i].pubkey == trustedSigner ... trustedSigners[i].expiresAt = 0;
findings.issue: The struct array at slot 0 is declared as an array based at slot 1 that only covers expiresAt (stor1[i].field_0 = slot 1 + 2i), while pubkey, member 0 of the same elements, stays raw stor[2 * i]; the two members of one array element read as unrelated storage.
findings.rule: When accesses stor[k*i + c] with the same index i use several offsets c < k, choose the base that makes them all members of one k-slot struct array (base 0: field_0 and field_256) instead of a base that turns one offset into the array start.

findings.source: OpenZeppelin Initializable v5 (ERC-7201 slot 0xf0c57e16...6a00, uint64 _initialized, bool _initializing)
findings.issue: Same as c00209: the Initializable slot is factored as a constant times 3600 in the reads of _initialized (P1), and _initialized is split into uint8 + uint56.
findings.rule: Never factor a storage slot by a time unit; merge field splits that no access reads separately.

notes: All 13 ABI functions reviewed (small UUPS/Ownable contract read in full). The 4 source loops (updateTrustedSigner's remove, update and insert loops; isValidSigner, inlined again in verifyUpdate) are clear whiles over the 100-element array ('while uint8(s) < 100') with their early returns and reverts ('no such pubkey', 'no space for new signer') exact.
summary: Faithful, with every loop a clear while; the signer array's two members are split between a mis-based stor1 and raw slots, and the Initializable slot is printed as a constant times 3600.
